supplement.where: Appendix A to L at the end of this PDF (pp. 46-59). Preregistrations at osf.io/jfzha and osf.io/95dhu (p. 11, footnote 1).
supplement.holds: Table A (Big Five balance), Table B (productivity with and without demographics, team level), Table C (work actions), Table D (message categories), Table E (ad copy completion), Table G (human ratings with process covariates), Table H (GPT-4o-mini ratings), Table I (field VTR and VTD), prompts. No separate online supplement is mentioned.

paper_design_summary: US Prolific participants were randomized on entry to work for 40 minutes either with another human participant (human-human team) or with a GPT-4o agent that could chat, edit ad copy, select and generate images (human-AI team), producing as many display ads for a think tank as they could. Both arms could generate images with DALL-E 3. The ads were scored by a separate sample of Prolific raters (text quality, image appeal, click likelihood), by GPT-4o-mini, by embedding distance to the condition centroid (diversity), and in a field campaign on X (CTR, CPC, view-through).

studies.label: Pairit ad-creation experiment (human-AI vs human-human teams) with rater evaluation and X field campaign

assignment.what_was_assigned: Partner type: a GPT-4o AI agent (human-AI team) or another human participant (human-human team)
assignment.quote: As soon as a participant was redirected to our platform from Prolific, they were randomized into either the human-human or the human-AI condition (Figure 2A).
assignment.locator: p. 14, Section 3.3 (AI randomization and queuing), Figure 2
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 11, Section 3 and footnote 1 (osf.io/jfzha, osf.io/95dhu); p. 18, Section 3.9 (field campaign preregistered on osf.io/95dhu)

arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: Participant paired with a gpt-4o-2024-08-06 agent with full workspace context that could send messages, edit headline/primary text/description, select images and generate DALL-E 3 images (not submit). Partner identity not revealed until the post-task survey.

arms.name: Human-Human
arms.description: Participant paired with another human participant in the same shared workspace; DALL-E 3 image generation was also available in this arm.

participants.exclusions: 2,500 preregistered and entered; 23 did not enter the matching queue and were removed; 167 quit or timed out before being matched; 2,310 completed the task; participants in 83 human-human sessions (14% of HH teams) whose partner did not complete were excluded from all analyses; final 2,234 (1,258 human-AI, 976 human-human); overall attrition 8.9%. The paper gives no count at assignment by arm. Diversity analysis restricted to 2,034 participants who submitted at least one ad with text. 85% completed the post-task survey.
participants.who: US adults on Prolific with representative stratification across gender and ethnicity; mean age 42 (SD 14); paid $9 plus a chance at $100 prizes
participants.quote: we exclude them from all analyses, yielding a final sample of 2,234 participants (1,258 human-AI, 976 human-human). The overall attrition rate was 8.9%.

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI gpt-4o-2024-08-06 as the agent (prompted every 10 seconds, chain-of-thought via structured outputs); DALL-E 3 image generation available to humans and agent in both arms
ai_tool.how_used: Agentic teammate in a shared real-time workspace: chats with the participant, writes and edits ad copy, selects stock images, generates DALL-E 3 images; only the human can submit ads (pp. 11-13, Sections 3.1-3.2).

task.description: Create display ads (headline, primary text, description, image) promoting a think tank's 2024 annual report; incentive of $100 prizes for quantity and quality of ads and field performance.
task.duration: 40 minutes for the ad task; median 46.32 minutes for the whole study (pp. 14-15)

outcomes.name: Text quality (human ratings)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 7-point Likert item 'The text is present, clear, relevant, and engaging', rated on ad mockups by a separate Prolific sample (each rater saw 40 ads; at least 3 ratings per ad). Regression at rating level with demographic controls; SE clustered at the ad level. Robustness: Table G adds process covariates (submissions, AI images, messages, edits).

contrasts.reported: Human-AI 0.327*** (0.024); Intercept 5.011*** (0.038); Demographics Yes; Observations 45803. With full covariates (Table G col. 2): Human-AI 0.432*** (0.052).
contrasts.locator: p. 22, Table 2 (Quality: Text); p. 51, Table G

outcomes.name: Image quality (human ratings)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 7-point Likert item 'The image is visually appealing', same raters and model as S1-O1; SE clustered at the ad level. Robustness in Table G col. 4.

contrasts.reported: Human-AI -0.133*** (0.021); Intercept 4.666*** (0.034); Observations 45803. With full covariates (Table G col. 4): Human-AI -0.165*** (0.044).
contrasts.locator: p. 22, Table 2 (Quality: Image); p. 51, Table G

outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 7-point Likert item 'I am likely to click on this ad' (rater-predicted engagement with the whole ad); same raters and model as S1-O1. Robustness in Table G col. 6.

contrasts.reported: Human-AI -0.013 (0.021); Intercept 3.698*** (0.035); Observations 45803. With full covariates (Table G col. 6): Human-AI 0.027 (0.044).
contrasts.locator: p. 22, Table 2 (Quality: Click); p. 51, Table G

outcomes.name: Output diversity (ad copy distance to condition centroid)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Each submission's ad copy (headline, primary text, description) embedded; cosine distance from each submission to its own treatment group's centroid; averaged to the participant; higher = more diverse. Restricted to participants with at least one text ad (N = 2,034 of 2,234).

contrasts.reported: Human-AI -0.094*** (0.006); Intercept 0.303*** (0.010); Demographics Yes; Observations 2034. Text: beta = -0.094, p < 0.001.
contrasts.locator: p. 21, Section 3.10 (Output diversity); p. 22, Table 2 (Output Diversity); p. 23, Section 4.1

diversity_detail.metric: Cosine distance from each submission to its condition's centroid embedding, averaged per participant (higher = more diverse); sign as printed, no reversal needed
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each output against the centroid of all outputs in its own treatment group, then averaged within participant
diversity_detail.uncertainty: OLS on participant-level averages with demographic controls (Equation 1), heteroskedasticity-robust SEs (Table 2 notes); no clustering by team stated
diversity_detail.notes: Centroids are computed separately per arm, so each arm is measured against its own centroid. Human-human team members share a workspace; the paper does not say how jointly confirmed ads are attributed to the two members. Within human-AI teams, delegation predicts lower diversity (-0.083***, 0.012; N = 1222; p. 30, Table 6 Panel B), a correlational analysis.

outcomes.name: Productivity (ads submitted per participant)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of ad submissions by the participant in 40 minutes. Table B also reports no-demographics and team-level versions; Table E shows higher ad-copy completion rates in human-AI teams (headline 0.150***, primary text 0.169***, description 0.161***).

contrasts.reported: Human-AI 1.954*** (0.197); Intercept 4.601*** (0.346); Demographics Yes; Observations 2234. Without demographics: Human-AI 1.925*** (0.197), Intercept 3.850*** (0.129). Team level: Human-AI -1.847*** (0.315), Intercept 7.623*** (0.277), Observations 1751. Text: '50% more ads per worker'.
contrasts.locator: p. 22, Table 2 (Productivity); p. 47, Table B; p. 49, Table E

outcomes.question: with_ai

Lower CPC is better.

company_involvement.description: Authors are at Johns Hopkins and MIT; funded by the MIT Initiative on the Digital Economy. The agent, raters' AI judge, and embeddings are OpenAI models; the ads were for an unnamed think tank. No company author or company funding stated.

data_and_code.data_url: Not posted: 'The code and data are available upon request.' (p. 39)
data_and_code.code_url: Survey platform code 'available on GitHub' with no URL printed (p. 17, footnote 3); otherwise on request (p. 39)

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomized on entry to a GPT-4o agent partner or a human partner (p. 14); 2,234 people analyzed (1,258 vs 976; p. 15, Table 1); ads (an in-scope creative task) were scored by raters for quality and by embedding distance for diversity (p. 22, Table 2). The comparison is AI agent versus human partner (ai_vs_active), not AI versus working alone: the paper has no human-alone arm (p. 22, p. 37), and DALL-E 3 image generation was available in both arms (p. 11). No creativity or novelty rating; quality items only.

one_line_finding: Participants randomized to a GPT-4o agent partner rather than a human partner produced ads with higher rated text quality (+0.327, SE 0.024, 7-point scale), lower rated image quality (-0.133, SE 0.021), and less diverse ad copy (distance to condition centroid -0.094, SE 0.006, intercept 0.303), with 1.954 more ads per person (p. 22, Table 2).
open_questions: Table 1 lists 976 human-human individuals in 493 teams (493 x 2 = 986); the paper does not explain the 10-person gap (p. 16).

Rater sample: the text says a separate sample of 1,995 was recruited, then that 1,200 entered and 5 dropped out (p. 17); 1,300 samples of 40 ads were prepared. The number of raters actually used is unclear.
Field sampling says 2,000 ads were drawn 'from a total of 11,138 ads' (p. 18), while the dataset elsewhere has 11,024 ads (pp. 1, 16).
Participant counts at assignment by arm are not given; 2,500 entered and randomization occurred on entry, but some of the 23 + 167 dropouts may have occurred before or after assignment.

Rating-level SEs are clustered by ad, not by participant or team; participant-level outcomes (productivity, diversity) use robust SEs without clustering by team, though human-human partners share a session.
Both arms had DALL-E 3 access, so the contrast isolates the LLM agent partner versus a human partner, not generative AI versus none.
notes: Version on file is arXiv v3 (Feb 2026); its title says 'A Field Experiment' while the search record says 'Field Experiments'. Outcomes are quality and diversity, not creativity or novelty ratings. Mechanism analyses (communication, delegation, recognition; Tables 4-6) are correlational or within-arm and are not listed as outcomes. Field outcomes in Table 3 condition on the human quality ratings, which are themselves affected by treatment.
